_comment: Workflow #3: a dialogue with one session, expressed as actions.
The driver asks for a task; a session does it and authors its result as a
review surface; the driver's annotations come back as the next TURN of that
same session; an approve verdict ends it. No GitHub anywhere — board,
surfaces and sessions only, which is why running this is the strongest
agnosticism proof the engine has (config/actions-eval.json was the second).
One topic carries a task, and one key carries one dialogue:
cadre/tasks/task:<id>  — the whole exchange. A `command` opens it, each
turn writes a `signal`, and the verdict closes
it. Three commands share the topic and are told
apart by `target`, exactly as the pipeline tells
`stage:interrogate` from `stage:revise`:
target=task           the ask            (runnerlib/tasks.submit_task)
target=task:feedback  the driver's next turn, from a surface annotation
target=task:verdict   the driver's verdict, from the surface's form
target=task:handoff     the node event: `node` names the node that takes
the work next (verdict=route:<node> on a page, or
an agent's own handoff). One generic action in
config/actions-handoff.json starts whichever node
it names.
Every one of them carries `story` as well as `task` — the same id under two
names. `story` is what the spawn seam reads to route a spawn spec, and what
the node's command template substitutes; `task` is what this workflow calls
the thing. Duplicating the value here is cheaper than a second seam.
Round caps ride the existing machinery (engine_seam.refuse_past_cap counts
firings per key) and the causal-depth cap is the loop guard, as everywhere.
Deliberately NOT here: the turn latency escape hatch, and the
working-directory allowlist the design page asked for. `cwd` travels in the
payload so a spawner can refuse an unlisted root; nothing in this file can
express that check — the `where` vocabulary has no path predicate.

actions.name: task-requested
actions._why: S0 of a dialogue. A `command` on the tasks topic is the driver asking for work; the task node does it and authors the surface the driver will read. `no_event_for_key` on the tasks signal is the once-only guard — the same shape story-to-intake uses, so a re-submitted or replayed command cannot open a second session on the same key.

payload.note: round 1 — the session authors the surface

actions.name: task-feedback-resumes-the-session
actions._why: The driver annotated the surface, so the dialogue takes another turn. Same key, and the node that built the page — the event names it in `node`, so one action serves every node, including ones registered after this file was written. The spawn is a RESUME rather than a restart: `resume=session` in the payload is what the spawn seam reads to continue the run's session id (runs.session_args -> --resume) instead of minting a new one, so the next turn keeps the context of the last. The grammar has no resume verb; a spawn body plus a payload flag is how that is said here.

payload.note: driver feedback is the next turn

actions.name: task-approved-done
actions._why: The driver approved on the surface's verdict form: the dialogue is over. Nothing downstream fires — approval is the end of the workflow, not a trigger for more work (the same rule final-merged-story-done keeps for the pipeline). A `continue` verdict is not handled here on purpose: continuing IS a feedback turn, and the surface writes it as one.
